journeys.title: Facing Fear with God
journeys.description: From the first tremor of fear to Jesus' own peace.

steps.note: Fear tells you that you face this alone.
The honest starting point: admit the fear, turn it into trust.
God answers fear with five of His own words: with you, your God, strengthen, help, uphold.
The spirit you were given is named: power, love, and a sound mind.
The journey ends at the peace Jesus Himself leaves behind.

journeys.title: Peace Over Anxiety
journeys.description: From a racing mind to a guarded heart.

steps.note: Anxiety treats tomorrow as if you must carry it alone today.
Jesus confines your strength to today — grace arrives daily.
The exchange: anxiety out, requests in — with thanksgiving.
The peace that guards is the peace Jesus gives.
The result: hearts and minds kept through Christ Jesus.

journeys.title: Comfort in Grief
journeys.description: From the night of weeping to the morning of joy.

steps.note: Grief is love with nowhere to go; Scripture does not rush it.
The LORD draws nearest exactly at the broken point.
Weeping has a term limit: night. Joy has an appointment: morning.
He binds up wounds — not wounds generally, yours.
The last page of the Bible promises a day with no tears left.

journeys.title: You Are Not Alone
journeys.description: From the ache of aloneness to the promise of presence.

steps.note: Feeling alone and being alone are different things in Scripture.
Even in the valley, the second line of the song is 'thou art with me'.
God's presence is not an idea; it is the provision for the journey.
He said it after giving the hardest assignment: lo, I am with you alway.
Five small words that will not break: never leave, never forsake.

changes: Step 4: pres-always retargeted to promise pr-pres-2.

journeys.title: Received in Christ
journeys.description: From the sting of rejection to the security of welcome.

steps.note: Rejection writes a name over you that God never wrote.
Whoever comes to Him, He will in no wise cast out — KJV never stutters here.
In Christ Jesus: no condemnation is the first fact about you.
You are His workmanship — received, then crafted.
Rejection called you unwanted; redemption calls you 'mine'.

changes: Step 4: pr-ident-2 retargeted to identity id-workmanship.

journeys.title: Guidance in Uncertainty
journeys.description: From fog at the fork to a word behind you.

steps.note: Decisions paralyze when we trust our understanding instead of His.
The condition is trust over self-insight; the result is directed paths.
God instructs personally: I will guide thee with mine eye.
A word behind you at the exact fork: this is the way.
When wisdom runs out, asking is the plan — asked liberally, answered liberally.

journeys.title: Strength While Waiting
journeys.description: From the long middle to renewed strength.

steps.note: Waiting is not wasted time in God's economy.
Waiting on the LORD is itself an exchange: weariness for strength.
Mercies are rationed daily — great is His faithfulness.
The delay has not cancelled the completion.
Due season is a harvest appointment, not a vague hope.

journeys.title: Rest for the Weary
journeys.description: From heavy-laden to yoked and rested.

steps.note: Weariness is an invitation in disguise.
Jesus' invitation is addressed to the labouring, not the accomplished.
A Shepherd's care ends in 'I shall not want'.
Presence and rest travel together.
Goodness and mercy pursue — even into the house of the LORD for ever.

journeys.title: From Temptation to Forgiveness
journeys.description: From the test, through grace, to cleansing.

steps.note: Temptation overstates its power and understates God's.
God measures what reaches you — and always leaves a way out.
The throne you run to is a throne of grace.
Confession meets faithfulness: forgiven, cleansed.
The verdict after grace: no condemnation.

journeys.title: Trusting God for Provision
journeys.description: From the pressure of need to the peace of supply.

steps.note: Need narrows vision; the kingdom widens it again.
First things first — and the Father adds what is needed.
Shepherds feed; 'I shall not want' is arithmetic under His care.
Paul told givers that God supplies givers — keep sowing, keep trusting.
Sufficiency is the target: enough, always, for every good work.

flags: Step note "'I shall not want' is arithmetic under His care" may overstate; editorial check.

journeys.title: Trust in Sickness
journeys.description: From the sickbed to the God who healeth.

steps.note: Illness isolates; Scripture gathers.
He reveals Himself by name here: the LORD that healeth thee.
The stripes were carried before the sickness was.
He restores health to outcasts no one seeks after.
The same God forgives all and heals all — bless Him while you wait.

flags: Steps cite Exodus 15:26 (covenant with Israel) and Isaiah 53:5; check notes do not promise a guaranteed cure.
